intended_object: The cluster set C(f, U, w) of a map f on a set U at a point w: the set of values v such that v lies in the closure of f(V ∩ U) for every neighbourhood V of w, i.e. the values approached by f(z) as z → w inside U (Collingwood–Lohwater, Pommerenke). Inferred from the docstring and module documentation.
explanation: In Mathlib, `MapClusterPt v (𝓝[U] w) f` is defined as `ClusterPt v (map f (𝓝[U] w))`. This holds exactly when v lies in the closure of f '' s for every s in 𝓝[U] w. The sets V ∩ U (V a neighbourhood of w) form a basis of 𝓝[U] w, so the definition is ⋂_V closure(f(V ∩ U)), the textbook cluster set. Edge cases agree with the docstring: if w ∉ closure U the filter is ⊥ and the set is empty. If w ∈ U the filter is not punctured, so f(w) can contribute, which matches "approached from inside U". The classical case is w ∈ frontier U of an open domain, where w ∉ U, so the definition agrees with the classical boundary cluster set. It is stated for arbitrary topological spaces, the natural generality. A case-insensitive grep for clusterset/cluster_set finds nothing in Mathlib, and the module documentation also notes that Mathlib has no named counterpart.
